LANTERN LANE
An interactive fiction by Joshua Herzig-Marx
A tutorial adventure. Release 1 / MIT License
It is the evening of the Lamp Festival, and you are old Pell the lamplighter's apprentice. Pell has gone ahead to the square with a promise that the great street lamp will be lit before the last light fades. He has left you the job.
Pell's Doorstep
You stand on the worn stone step of the lamplighter's cottage. The front door is painted green and the paint is peeling. A clay flowerpot full of tired geraniums sits beside the step. Lantern Lane runs away to the north between low stone walls, and the sky above it is turning the colour of weak tea.
A chipped clay pot of geraniums. It sits slightly crooked, as though it has been moved a few times.

A stout cottage door with peeling green paint and a brass keyhole.
The green front door is closed.
You tip the flowerpot aside. Pressed into the damp earth beneath it lies a small brass key.

Taken.

[Your score has just gone up by 1 point.]

You unlock the green front door.

[Your score has just gone up by 1 point.]
You open the green front door.

Lamplighter's Kitchen
A snug, low-ceilinged kitchen smelling of oil and woodsmoke. A black stove squats in one corner, and above it runs a narrow mantel. A scrubbed table stands under the window. In the floor by the stove is a square trapdoor with an iron ring. The front door leads out to the doorstep.
A hurricane lantern hangs from a hook beside the stove.
On the scrubbed table you can see a folded note and a biscuit tin (closed).
On the mantel you can see a box of matches.
A folded sheet of paper, addressed in a neat hand: "For the apprentice."

"Apprentice -- I have gone ahead to the square. The great lamp wants filling and lighting before dusk is done.
The lamp oil is in the cellar, so you will need a light of your own down there: the lantern on its hook will serve, and the matches are on the mantel. The lamp itself is too high to reach, and the only ladder on the lane belongs to Bram, the baker's boy. He will swap it for something sweet. -- Pell"

[Your score has just gone up by 1 point.]
You open the biscuit tin, revealing a ginger biscuit.

You strike a match from the box and touch it to the wick. The lantern catches with a warm yellow glow.

[Your score has just gone up by 1 point.]

Cellar
A cool, low cellar with a floor of beaten earth. Barrels line one wall and stout shelves hold jars, rope and the usual lamplighter's clutter. A flight of steps leads back up to the kitchen.
A tin can of lamp oil stands on the nearest shelf.

Taken.

[Your score has just gone up by 1 point.]
Plain pine shelves holding jars, a coil of rope and assorted lamplighter's clutter. None of it is any use tonight.

Lamplighter's Kitchen
A snug, low-ceilinged kitchen smelling of oil and woodsmoke. A black stove squats in one corner, and above it runs a narrow mantel. A scrubbed table stands under the window. In the floor by the stove is a square trapdoor with an iron ring. The front door leads out to the doorstep.
On the scrubbed table you can see a folded note and a biscuit tin (open).

Pell's Doorstep
You stand on the worn stone step of the lamplighter's cottage. The front door is painted green and the paint is peeling. A clay flowerpot full of tired geraniums sits beside the step. Lantern Lane runs away to the north between low stone walls, and the sky above it is turning the colour of weak tea.

Lantern Lane
The lane is cobbled and crooked, and a row of iron lamp brackets, all of them lit already, marches off to the north. A low wall runs along the east side. Pell's cottage is to the south, and the lane opens into a square to the north.
Bram, the baker's boy, sits on the wall swinging his boots and looking hungry.
You can also see a wooden ladder here.

Bram's eyes go round. He takes the biscuit and has it down in two bites. "Go on, then," he says through the crumbs. "Take the ladder. Mind you bring it back."

[Your score has just gone up by 2 points.]

Lamplight Square
A small cobbled square with a dry fountain at its centre. At the north end stands the great street lamp on its tall iron post, its glass dark and cold. Everything else in the square glows with festival lanterns, but the great lamp is the one everyone will look to. The lane leads back south.
A tall iron post topped by a glass lamp as big as a barrel. The reservoir looks empty. It is far too high to reach from the ground.
You prop the ladder against the lamp post. It looks firm enough to climb.
You climb a few rungs and back down. Better to wait until there is something to do at the top.
You climb a few rungs and back down. Better to wait until there is something to do at the top.

You climb the ladder with the oil can, unscrew the little brass cap and tip oil into the lamp's reservoir until it is nearly full. Then you climb down again.

[Your score has just gone up by 1 point.]

You climb the ladder, strike a flame and hold it to the wick. For a moment nothing happens, then the lamp takes light.

[Your score has just gone up by 2 points.]

Gold light spills down the post and along the cobbles. One by one, up and down Lantern Lane, windows open and neighbours come out to stand beneath the glow. Old Pell, grinning, steps out from behind the baker's cart. "Not bad for a first night, apprentice," he says. "Not bad at all."

In that game you scored 10 out of a possible 10, in 30 moves.
